title: Best Mac Studio (2026)
summary: The guide ranks Apple’s Mac Studio lineup, focusing on the ultra‑powerful M5 Ultra and its more affordable siblings.
method: Picks were chosen by counting how many of the five source articles mention each model and by comparing the performance, port, and price details each source provides.
assumptions: All price figures come directly from the sources; no external pricing data was added.

products.name: Apple Mac Studio (M5 Ultra)
why: The Verge notes the M5 Ultra model has a 36‑core CPU, 80‑core GPU, 256 GB RAM and 4 TB storage, costing $12,299. CNET calls it “really, really fast and quiet” and highlights its compact design.
TechRadar and CNET both point out that the M5 Ultra cannot be upgraded after purchase and that it is the most expensive configuration in the lineup.
products.desc: A compact desktop with a 36‑core CPU, 80‑core GPU, up to 256 GB RAM and up to 4 TB storage. It includes many Thunderbolt ports and runs quietly, but memory cannot be upgraded later.
products.best_for: AI developers and high‑end 3D VFX studios
products.amazon_listing: Apple 2026 Mac Studio desktop computer M5 Ultra chip | A powerful platform for AI, with 30

products.name: Apple Mac Studio (M5 Max)
why: The Verge lists the M5 Max as an alternative to the Ultra, using the same chassis but with fewer Thunderbolt connections.
CNET notes the M5 Max is slightly less expensive than the Ultra and still offers strong performance for demanding tasks.
products.desc: Uses the same compact design as the Ultra but with a slightly lower‑spec chip and two fewer Thunderbolt ports. It still provides high‑end CPU/GPU performance and quiet operation.
products.benefit: Picture a freelance video editor needing fast renders without breaking the bank. The M5 Max delivers strong performance and many ports, beating the M4 Max’s older chip and the M1 Ultra’s older architecture while costing less than the Ultra. The catch: it still lacks memory upgrade options and has fewer Thunderbolt connections than the Ultra.
specs: Multiple Thunderbolt ports (two fewer than Ultra)
products.best_for: Professional creators who need power but have a tighter budget
products.skip_if: You need the absolute top‑tier specs

products.name: Apple Mac Studio (M4 Max)
why: PCMag highlights the M4 Max model for its “powerful performance for productivity, graphics, and workstation tasks” and notes Thunderbolt 5 connectivity.
PCMag also mentions the lack of internal upgradability and that it starts at $1,999 (now $2,499 after a price increase).
products.desc: A compact desktop with an M4 Max chip, Thunderbolt 5 ports, and whisper‑quiet cooling. It does not include Wi‑Fi 7 and cannot be upgraded internally.
products.benefit: Picture a small design studio needing solid performance for everyday tasks. The M4 Max offers strong CPU and GPU capability, the newest Thunderbolt 5 ports and a lower entry price than the M5 models, making it the most affordable option in this guide. The catch: it lacks Wi‑Fi 7 and cannot be upgraded after purchase.
products.best_for: Small teams or individuals seeking a capable Mac desktop without premium cost
products.skip_if: You need the highest possible CPU/GPU power

products.name: Apple Mac Studio (M1 Ultra)
why: Tom's Guide calls the M1 Ultra version “blazing‑fast performance” and praises its design and port selection.
TechRadar includes the M1 Ultra in its comparison of newer models, noting it still offers strong CPU/GPU power.
products.desc: A compact desktop featuring the M1 Ultra chip, many ports and a quiet chassis. It is older than the M4/M5 models but still delivers high performance.
products.benefit: Picture a university lab needing a reliable workstation for mixed workloads. The M1 Ultra provides fast CPU/GPU performance and many ports, outpacing the older M4 Max in raw speed while costing less than the newer M5 Max. The catch: it is an older generation and may lack the newest connectivity like Thunderbolt 5.
products.best_for: Users who want strong performance but don’t need the latest M5 features
products.skip_if: You want the newest CPU/GPU architecture
